title: The current official count of IICs is unverifiable
what_we_know: Last official PIB figure is 'more than 6,400' in Nov 2022 (GOV-006). MIC Brochure 2025 contains a national IIC count embedded as a vector graphic that did not survive PDF text extraction. A media claim of 'over 14,000 HEIs' (Education Times, Feb 2025) is implausible against 6,400 and is not a verifiable attribution.
why_it_blocks: This is the single most important denominator in the project - the closest proxy for 'how many Indian institutions have a functioning innovation structure'.
what_would_settle_it: Authenticated access to iic.mic.gov.in/institute-list; manual read of the MIC Brochure 2025 graphic; written query to MIC (mic-mhrd@gov.in); or an RTI.
interim_handling: Cite 6,400 with its 2022 date, never the current count. All market sizing must be shown both with and without IIC coverage.

title: AICTE total approved institutions and the engineering-college-specific count
what_we_know: PRS compiled 8,489 technical institutions as of April 2026 (Tier 2). AICTE's Analytics Dashboard returned HTTP 404 and a search snippet showed '12,981 institutes' that could not be attributed to an academic year (filters spanned 2012-13 to 2026-27). Engineering-college-only count is unknown; AICTE publishes only bulk-login downloads.
why_it_blocks: Engineering colleges are a named segment in todo.md Phase 4. Sizing them requires the true count.
what_would_settle_it: AICTE Centralized Support System login, or the annual approved-institution list.
interim_handling: Use 8,489 with a Tier-2 caveat. Never cite 12,981.

title: Willingness to pay - completely unvalidated
what_we_know: We have competitor prices (Rs 75k-6.25L/yr) and free-tier anchors (Rs 0-1.73L/yr). We have ZERO primary evidence of what an institution would actually pay. todo.md carries an assumed Rs 1.2L/yr with no source - and it sits ABOVE the cheapest credible Indian incumbent.
why_it_blocks: Phases 7, 8, 16, 17 and 18 all depend on it. A financial model built on Rs 1.2L is currently an assertion, not a model.
what_would_settle_it: Phase 3 interviews (10-15 institutions) using the VALUE framing - 'if this problem disappeared tomorrow, what would that save you?' - not 'would you pay Rs 1.2 lakh?'. Plus Phase 20 pilot conversion data.
interim_handling: Treat Rs 75,000 as a COMPETITIVE anchor, not a pricing decision.

title: No public API anywhere in the mandated stack
what_we_know: No public API, developer documentation or bulk export endpoint found for IIC, YUKTI, NIRF, AISHE or MAARG (GOV-043). All are form-based web apps with per-activity manual uploads. data.gov.in carries some DPIIT/CSVs but they are parliamentary-answer snapshots, not live APIs; the Startup India SRF CSV returns 'Session Expired' on unauthenticated fetch.
why_it_blocks: If these systems have no APIs, integration is impossible and must be reimplemented as export-then-import. This changes the technical architecture (Phase 22) AND the pitch (one-click export, not live sync).
what_would_settle_it: Written enquiry to MIC/MoE, or an RTI.

title: Four rival datasets disagree on AIC count, three on TBI count
what_we_know: AIC: 83 (Lok Sabha Mar 2026) / 72 (AIM site) / 69 (AIM AIC page Jan 2024). TBI: 'more than 160' (DST) / '175+' (PIB Jan 2026) / 164 (ISTI). BioNEST: 74 (stats block) / 75 (table footer) on the SAME page. IIC: 6,400 (PIB 2022) / unreadable (MIC Brochure 2025) / '14,000' (media).
why_it_blocks: Presenting a single number without its source and date is how market sizing becomes indefensible.
what_would_settle_it: See OQ-01 for the IIC figure. Others need MIC and DST written confirmation.
interim_handling: Never present a single number without source and date. Where a range matters, present the range. Use 83 for AIC.

title: UGC and AISHE use different frames for 'university'
what_we_know: UGC (31.03.2024): 57 Central / 482 State Public / 478 State Private / 136 Deemed = 1,153. AISHE (2023-24): 55 / 462 / 464 / 125 = 1,289.
why_it_blocks: Mixing the frames produces a wrong total. Comparing them produces a false discrepancy.
what_would_settle_it: Nothing - the frames are genuinely different, not one being wrong. This is permanent.
interim_handling: Keep the frames separate. Never cite '1,289 universities' without the year and frame.

title: Autonomous college count
what_we_know: Only 578/579 appears, on an AISHE dashboard whose vintage is unlabelled and whose college counts exceed the published 2023-24 totals. UGC publishes no authoritative total. UGC issued the UGC (Conferment of Autonomous Status upon Colleges) Regulations, 2023.
why_it_blocks: Autonomous colleges are a named segment in todo.md Phase 4.
what_would_settle_it: UGC autonomous-college register or an RTI.

title: Incubator/accelerator counts on Startup India are login-gated
what_we_know: BHASKAR's incubator and accelerator listings publish no aggregate count. The only public figure is a '600K strong' registry counter, which is NOT an incubator count and is marketing. Closest official national aggregate: MeitY Startup Hub 517+ incubators (Dec 2025, GOV-012). Per-state incubator counts are published by nobody.
why_it_blocks: todo.md Phase 5 asks for incubator and accelerator counts. They do not exist publicly.
what_would_settle_it: Authenticated BHASKAR access, or a DPIIT RTI.
interim_handling: Use 517+ with the MeitY attribution and state the limitation.

title: Almost no independent review evidence exists in this market
what_we_know: Six of eleven direct competitors have ZERO third-party reviews. Gohorto: 3 GetApp, one vendor-referred. Founderhood: 1 G2 + 2 Capterra. AcceleratorApp: none found. incuTrack: 10 G2 (3.8), recent ones 'quite outdated'. Accubate: 26 Capterra (4.8) - the only real base. Consequence: nobody can prove a large Indian institution runs on their software.
why_it_blocks: todo.md Phase 11 (competitor user reviews) is THIN BY NECESSITY, not omission. Also: all G2/Capterra quotes come from search-index excerpts because both sites 403 automated fetch.
what_would_settle_it: Direct re-verification of any quote before customer-facing use. Longer-term: one published StartupHub case study with named referees.
interim_handling: Treat all review quotes as Tier 4. Re-verify before external use.

title: IIC's star-rating formula is not publicly documented
what_we_know: The official 'Rating and Scoring System' help page returns 'Coming Soon' (GOV-044). 3-star and 5-star ratings appear in institutional reports, so the system exists and works, but weights and thresholds are unknown.
why_it_blocks: FEATURE RISK. If StartupHub's core promise is 'your IIC data is already here, here's your star rating', we cannot build it without the formula.
what_would_settle_it: MIC clarification, or reverse-engineering from institutional Performance Cards across many years.
interim_handling: Do not promise star-rating prediction in V1.

title: BHASKAR overhaul - real threat or press noise?
what_we_know: DPIIT reportedly plans to turn BHASKAR into a 'National Startup Master Data' registry tracking the startup lifecycle; MeitY Startup Hub floated a similar tender (GOV-040, 21 May 2026, Moneycontrol). Tier 4 - trade press reporting a plan, not a notification.
why_it_blocks: If a national master data layer materialises, it becomes the upstream identity system and StartupHub must reconcile to it rather than duplicate it.
what_would_settle_it: A published tender document or government notification.
interim_handling: Design for BHASKAR-ID reconciliation now. Do NOT cite externally until confirmed from a government source. Re-check before any launch.

title: No peer-reviewed literature on Indian institutional reporting burden
what_we_know: Searched and NOT FOUND. What exists instead: ARIIA's own DCS statement that integration 'has reduced data submission efforts at the institute level by checking redundancy' (GOV-031); the AISHE 2023-24 report enumerating 12+ HEI-facing portals (GOV-006); RBI's SDMX paper as an analogy; NIRF methodology critiques that focus on ranking validity, not data-entry burden.
why_it_blocks: No one has quantified this burden. StartupHub should run its own primary time-and-motion study across ~20 IIC institutions.
what_would_settle_it: Our own primary research - Phase 3 interviews plus a structured time-and-motion study.
interim_handling: A genuinely novel research opportunity. It is the difference between 'institutions have this problem' and '7 of 10 lose X hours per month to it'.

title: Whether an institution-facing product can even be bought easily
what_we_know: Not yet researched. GeM procurement route (eligibility, registration, listing mechanics, security-questionnaire burden); DRE/Direct Purchase rules; data-localisation and on-premise requirements as procurement conditions; whether an IIC can sign a SaaS contract or needs the university as contracting party.
why_it_blocks: May be the hardest constraint in the business. EcoSync has already publicly conceded no SOC 2 / ISO 27001 and no uptime SLA - procurement is a real moat if StartupHub can clear it.
what_would_settle_it: Phase 24 legal/compliance + Phase 19 GTM, plus talking to 2-3 institutional procurement officers.
interim_handling: Assume procurement is slow and evidence-heavy. Build the compliance output as an asset, not an afterthought.

title: The list of 31 States/UTs with a dedicated Startup Policy is login-gated
what_we_know: The count (31 of 36, as of 14 Sep 2026) is published; the list is not extractable. UP's Startup Policy 2026 was approved by State Cabinet on 6 July 2026, replacing the 2020 policy. Delhi, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and UP institution-facing portals were NOT verified in this pass.
why_it_blocks: State policy coverage is a Phase 27 input and a Phase 19 partner-mapping input.
what_would_settle_it: State government gazette archives; Startup India SRF participation records.
interim_handling: Cite the count, not the list.

title: University/technology-transfer software only partly researched
what_we_know: Elsevier Pure is well documented and priced (COMP-014) - minimum Indian deployment ~Rs 44.6L/yr + Rs 43.5L onboarding, roughly two orders of magnitude above StartupHub's band. But Invenio, Tech Transfer Ware, and the university innovation-management category were only lightly covered. A university CTO could argue 'we already own Pure'.
why_it_blocks: Innoloft's LoftOS case study (RWTH Aachen Collaeb) shows universities DO build and buy this category.
what_would_settle_it: Phase 22 task: Invenio, Tech Transfer Ware, and the university TTO software category.
interim_handling: Note Pure as a procurement objection, not a feature competitor.

title: Hindi / regional-language UI is claimed by almost nobody
what_we_know: Only Accubate lists Hindi as supported (on GetApp). Orbit's Sarvam-based Indian-language MOM transcription is the one genuinely India-specific AI feature found anywhere in the category. AcceleratorApp translates into seven European languages, Arabic and Ukrainian, but NOT Hindi.
why_it_blocks: If council meetings and mentor sessions happen in Malayalam/Tamil/Marathi, language could be a wedge or a non-issue. Nobody should guess.
what_would_settle_it: Phase 3 interview question, not an assumption.
interim_handling: Ask in interviews. Do not build on it yet.

title: Campus ERP channel risk
what_we_know: Zero Indian campus ERP vendors have a genuine startup-incubation module (COMP-021), but several already claim 'NAAC SSR auto-generation, NIRF ranking data, AISHE submissions' (OnCampusERP, EduplusCampus). They compete for the compliance budget, own the institutional relationship, and hold the procurement precedent. Jaraka/Habbinson sells 'Institutional Excellence and IIC' as a module alongside its ERP.
why_it_blocks: A Phase 19 question: is StartupHub a partner, a competitor, or a module they'd resell?
what_would_settle_it: Phase 19 GTM. Conversations with 2-3 ERP vendors.
interim_handling: Track them. Most likely a channel, not a competitor.

title: Incu (Sweden) tracks patents as a data field
what_we_know: 'Moduler med nyckeldata om avtal, patent, kapital, varumarke' - 790 kr/user/month (~US$75) + EUR 3,500 implementation. The ONLY competitor found anywhere with any patent awareness.
why_it_blocks: If its patent module is deeper than a field, it partially invalidates GAP-01's 'zero competitors' framing.
what_would_settle_it: A direct look at Incu's product and feature list.
interim_handling: GAP-01 stands unless Incu demonstrably has a patent WORKFLOW.
